source: Lichtenstein

source: Kenneth Martin (P5 order)
mechanism: rule-based line-bundle compositions in HTML/CSS/JS

title: The webpage going on and off
source: Martin Creed, Work No. 227 (P1)
mechanism: page cycles white 7s / black 10s forever via the render loop

title: But is it art?
source: the eternal question (P3)
mechanism: a page that displays one word: YES

title: Tragedian
source: Cattelan, Comedian (P2)
mechanism: morphing photoreal fruit + duct tape that vanishes on touch

title: Images That Never Were
source: art-vandalism history + AI (P10)
mechanism: cinematic AI tableaux of undocumented art attacks

title: Andy Warhol eating a hamburger (SVG)
source: Warhol + Willison SVG-benchmark (P10)
mechanism: LLM-generated SVGs compared across models, on Warhol color-bands

title: The Original
source: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art
mechanism: Client-side Blob download of the page's own source plus a private localStorage edition counter that exposes scarcity as fiction.

title: The Unkept
source: Tino Sehgal; constructed situations / no documentation
mechanism: Page Visibility API plus window blur/pagehide events irrevocably kill a live canvas render; deliberately no storage, cache, or persistence.

title: Today
source: On Kawara, Today series (Date Paintings), 1966-2013
mechanism: Per-visit render of today's date via Intl locale formatting (Esperanto fallback for non-Roman scripts), with a setInterval counting down to local midnight that repaints and discards the painting — zero persistence, zero external requests.

title: Wall Drawing for No Wall
source: Sol LeWitt, Wall Drawings; Sol LeWitt, Paragraphs on Conceptual Art (1967)
mechanism: Client-side JS executes a printed LeWitt-style instruction live per visit, generating the instruction text and the drawing from the same parameters; each load/click is a new draftsman, erased on navigation.

source: Roman Opałka, OPAŁKA 1965 / 1 – ∞ (Détails); On Kawara, I Am Still Alive
mechanism: requestAnimationFrame increments an integer while a tint function interpolates its colour toward the page background as a function of the same count; no persistence, no network, reload restarts at 1.

title: Composition in Red, Yellow and Blue (32 × 32)
source: Piet Mondrian, Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow (c. 1930); net.art (browser chrome as material)
mechanism: Canvas-drawn recursive Mondrian set as the favicon via toDataURL + <link rel=icon>; the browser's mandatory 32px raster is Mondrian's grid.

title: Page with the Sound of Its Own Making
source: Robert Morris, Box with the Sound of Its Own Making (1961); process art; net.art (page as its own medium)
mechanism: Web Audio API sonifies document.documentElement.outerHTML one character at a time, client-side, no recording and no network; the source it sings includes the script doing the singing.

title: Erased (No Undo)
source: Robert Rauschenberg, Erased de Kooning Drawing (1953); Willem de Kooning; Marcel Duchamp / the readymade
mechanism: Destructive canvas compositing (destination-out) you perform by hand, with the erased state written irreversibly to localStorage and Ctrl+Z refused — the web's undo withheld.

title: If I Say So
source: Robert Rauschenberg, This Is a Portrait of Iris Clert If I Say So (1961); net.art (the URL as material)
mechanism: The sitter is bound to location.hash; saying-so becomes typing the address bar, read live on hashchange.

title: Linea
source: Piero Manzoni, Linea (1959–60); Piero Manzoni, Linea m 7,200 (Herning, 1960); Marcel Duchamp / infrathin
mechanism: Per-visit JS generates a real normalised polyline of the labelled length but never renders it to DOM or canvas; the console attests it, no surface shows it.

title: One and Three Chairs (HTTP)
source: Joseph Kosuth, One and Three Chairs (1965); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); net.art
mechanism: A live unknown <chair> HTML element renders as nothing beside a per-visit procedurally generated SVG chair and a fixed dictionary definition; absence is structural, attested in console.

title: Abstract Painting (Backlit)
source: Ad Reinhardt, Abstract Painting (1960-66); Ad Reinhardt, Art-as-Art dogma; Kazimir Malevich, Black Square (1915); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: Canvas renders a near-threshold tinted black cross with no fixed per-device appearance; an on-demand canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg',0.4) round-trip quantizes the colored blacks back to nothing, enacting reproduction-as-erasure live and client-side.

title: Zone de Sensibilité Picturale Immatérielle (Web Series)
source: Yves Klein, Zones of Immaterial Pictorial Sensibility (1959-1962); Yves Klein, the receipt-burning ritual on the Seine (1962)
mechanism: A per-visit JS-minted receipt with a unique serial held only in closure; 'burn' irreversibly nulls it and the page persists nothing (no storage, cookies, server, or token), so reload shows no transaction ever existed.

title: Perfect Lovers (Reset)
source: Félix González-Torres, "Untitled" (Perfect Lovers), 1991; net.art (browser timer drift as material)
mechanism: requestAnimationFrame advances two clocks at slightly different rates with a battery-depletion model and no resync to real time; reload re-sets them to the same time.

title: Each Being Equal
source: Lawrence Weiner, Declaration of Intent (1968); Conceptual art / language-as-material; net.art
mechanism: Per-visit JS grammar mints a statement and declares it complete on receipt; the offered condition buttons resolve to no material change, enacting 'each being equal' as a dead call-to-action.

title: 4′33″ (We Do Not Listen)
source: John Cage, 4′33″ (1952); David Tudor, Woodstock première (1952)
mechanism: A requestAnimationFrame transport plays three timed tacet movements while deliberately creating no AudioContext, no getUserMedia, and no network request; the absence of capture is the performed silence.

title: 1000 Hours of Staring
source: Tom Friedman, 1000 Hours of Staring (1992-1997); On Kawara, Today series; Roman Opalka, 1965 / 1 – ∞
mechanism: document.visibilityState + document.hasFocus() gate a time accumulator persisted only in localStorage; attention becomes the unprovable, unsellable medium.

title: this way browser
source: Stanley Brouwn, this way brouwn (1961); Stanley Brouwn, the distance / step works; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: Pointer Events (mouse, pen and touch) deltas summed and converted to physical distance via the CSS reference pixel (1/96 inch); touch-action:none claims the gesture so a finger-drag walks on mobile; no rendering of the path, no storage, no network.

title: Measurement: Viewport
source: Mel Bochner, Measurement: Room (1969); Mel Bochner, Measurement Series (1968-69); net.art (viewport as material)
mechanism: window.innerWidth/innerHeight (and devicePixelRatio) read live and redrawn as arrowed dimension lines on every resize; no fixed size, nothing stored, no network.

title: The Vertical Earth Kilometer
source: Walter De Maria, The Vertical Earth Kilometer (1977), Friedrichsplatz, Kassel
mechanism: A document with height:100000cm (one real CSS kilometre, ~3.78M px); a probe element measures the browser's own metre and a scroll handler reports depth, while the rod itself is never drawn.

title: Random Distribution of π
source: François Morellet, Répartition aléatoire de 40 000 carrés suivant les chiffres pairs et impairs d'un annuaire de téléphone (1960); Kenneth Martin, Chance and Order; π / the unbounded spigot algorithm (Gibbons, 2004)
mechanism: An unbounded BigInt spigot streams the exact decimal digits of π client-side; each digit's parity fills or clears a square in a grid extended infinitely on scroll — deterministic, identical in every browser, no network.

title: Oil on Viewer
source: Hans Haacke, Condensation Cube (1963-65); Laszlo Moholy-Nagy, Telephone Pictures (1922); net.art (OS/browser as material)
mechanism: matchMedia preference queries (prefers-color-scheme/contrast/reduced-motion/inverted-colors/forced-colors/color-gamut/dynamic-range) with live change events drive CSS custom properties and a Haacke-style real-time data plate; no controls, no storage, no network.

title: The Blackest Black (available to everyone, including Anish Kapoor)
source: Anish Kapoor / Vantablack exclusive licence (2016); Stuart Semple, Black 2.0/3.0 and the Pinkest Pink ('except Anish Kapoor'); Kazimir Malevich, Black Square (1915); Ad Reinhardt, black paintings; net.art / the costless copy
mechanism: Click triggers a local navigator.clipboard.writeText('#000000') that transfers the work's whole material to the viewer; the device's maximal switched-off black plus an open-licence label, no network or storage.

title: Oral Communication
source: Ian Wilson, Oral Communication / The Discussions (1968– ); conceptual art / dematerialization of the art object; net.art (the browser as a copy machine made not to copy)
mechanism: Local Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis, offline-preferred voice) recites a JS-only string never inserted into the DOM, deliberately paired with the absence of recording, storage, and network.

title: Subway Drawing (any line)
source: William Anastasi, Subway Drawings (1960s–); William Anastasi, Pocket Drawings; Surrealist automatic drawing
mechanism: DeviceMotionEvent accelerometer (high-pass filtered) drives a canvas polyline; iOS motion-permission gesture; no storage, no network, reload erases.

title: During the Connection the Gallery Will Be Closed
source: Robert Barry, During the exhibition the gallery will be closed (1969); Lee Lozano, General Strike Piece (1969); net.art
mechanism: navigator.onLine plus online/offline events toggle the page between a closed and an open gallery; no requests, no storage.

title: Equivalent (Any of the Fourteen)
source: Carl Andre, Equivalent VIII (1966); Carl Andre, Equivalent I–VIII (1966); Tate acquisition / the 'pile of bricks' press scandal (1972/1976); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade
mechanism: Per-click client-side DOM re-render that varies only the rectangular footprint while the brick count stays hard-coded and constant; the footprints are computed by factoring a divisor-rich number (180) under Andre's shortest-side-≥-3 rule; no storage, no network.

title: Acid Action Painting (Reload to Resurrect)
source: Gustav Metzger, Acid Action Painting (1960); Gustav Metzger, Auto-Destructive Art manifesto (1959); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Jean Tinguely, Homage to New York (1960)
mechanism: Per-visit requestAnimationFrame removes real DOM cells in a chance-shuffled order over a declared finite lifespan, then strips every element under <body> — picture, label, and the script's own node — leaving an empty document; the only surviving trace is the <title> in the head, flipped to '(deleted — reload to resurrect)'; reload restores a perfect copy; no storage, no network.

title: 148 Colours
source: Gerhard Richter, 1024 Colours (1974); Gerhard Richter, 256 Colours / 4096 Colours; Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; CSS Color Module Level 4 named colours (W3C)
mechanism: The CSS Color Module Level 4 named-colour list is rendered swatch by swatch with backgroundColor and read back via getComputedStyle, chance-shuffled per visit; the engine supplies every pixel, nothing is stored, no network.

title: An Artist Who Cannot Speak English Is No Artist
source: Mladen Stilinovic, An Artist Who Cannot Speak English Is No Artist (1992); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art (navigator.languages as material)
mechanism: Client-side read of navigator.languages issues a per-visit 'artist / no artist' verdict; nothing sent, stored, or tracked, and the gate is gameable by editing one browser preference.

title: Suitable for Framing
source: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Seth Siegelaub, Xerox Book / catalogue-as-exhibition (1968)
mechanism: A @media print stylesheet hides every element (body * display:none) and lets only a body::after epitaph through, so reproduction onto paper returns nothing; per-visit hues via client-side Math.random, no storage or network.

title: Certificate of Authenticity
source: Donald Judd, certificates of authenticity; Dan Flavin, certificates / fabricated multiples; the NFT / blockchain authenticity discourse; Marcel Duchamp, infrathin; W3C Web Crypto API (SubtleCrypto)
mechanism: Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle SHA-256) hashes document.documentElement.outerHTML per visit and stamps the digest into the page; a re-hash proves the certificate is stale the instant it is issued.

title: The Death of the Author
source: Roland Barthes, The Death of the Author (1967); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art (contenteditable / the DOM as material)
mechanism: A contenteditable article whose first beforeinput event strikes the author byline and reassigns the page to the reader; nothing persisted, so reload restores the original author.

title: Entropy (Black Sand, White Sand)
source: Robert Smithson, Entropy and the New Monuments (1966); Robert Smithson, the sandbox parable; net.art (browser canvas as material)
mechanism: Pointer-driven, sand-conserving neighbour-swaps on a canvas grid with a live boundary-count disorder meter that only climbs; reload is the sole reset, no storage, no network.

title: Inside the White Cube
source: Brian O'Doherty, Inside the White Cube: The Ideology of the Gallery Space (1976); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art (browser chrome / Fullscreen API as material)
mechanism: Fullscreen API strips all browser/OS chrome on demand, enacting the white cube's context-erasure; fullscreenchange toggles the 'Now it is art' verdict, with a faux-cube fallback when the request is refused; per-visit hue via Math.random.

title: Hierarchy of Genres
source: Andre Felibien, Preface aux Conferences de l'Academie royale (1667) — the hierarchy of genres; the academic genres: history painting, portrait, landscape, still life; Mel Bochner, Measurement series (1968-69); net.art (screen orientation as material)
mechanism: Viewport aspect ratio via resize/orientationchange (the @media-orientation pun: portrait vs landscape) maps the rectangle's orientation onto Felibien's 1667 ranking of genres, redrawing the canvas and wall label per turn; per-visit hue via Math.random, no storage, no network.

title: Changes You Made May Not Be Saved
source: Bas Jan Ader, I'm too sad to tell you (1971); y-a-v-a, i-m-too-sad-to-tell-you (2012); browser vendors' deprecation of custom beforeunload messages (~2016)
mechanism: The beforeunload event's returnValue is set to a per-visit farewell and ignored by browsers (custom strings deprecated ~2016), which speak a fixed corporate line instead.

title: Optical Mixture
source: Georges Seurat, Un dimanche apres-midi a l'Ile de la Grande Jatte (1884-86); Paul Signac / pointillism / divisionism; Chevreul, law of simultaneous contrast
mechanism: Live zoom detection (visualViewport.scale + devicePixelRatio baseline) drives a deterministic complementary-dot canvas apart as the viewer looks closer, so leaning in dissolves the optical mixture; no storage, no network.

title: Time Clock Piece (You Will Miss the Next One)
source: Tehching Hsieh, One Year Performance 1980-1981 (Time Clock Piece); On Kawara, Today series
mechanism: A punch button gated to the first 60 seconds of each clock hour, with a localStorage-anchored year-grid (8,760 cells) that retroactively marks every elapsed un-punched hour as a permanent miss; system clock only, no network.

title: Inert Gas (From a Measured Volume to Indefinite Expansion)
source: Robert Barry, Inert Gas Series (1969); Robert Barry, From a Measured Volume to Indefinite Expansion (1969); conceptual art / dematerialization of the art object; net.art (the accessibility tree / DOM as material)
mechanism: The HTML inert attribute progressively removes each gas element from pointer events, the focus order and the accessibility tree (present in the DOM, unreachable), then inerts the whole apparatus; reload refills; no storage, no network.

title: Pure Colour
source: Aleksandr Rodchenko, Pure Red Colour / Pure Yellow Colour / Pure Blue Colour (1921); the monochrome / end-of-painting tradition; net.art (browser & OS chrome as material)
mechanism: A live <input type="color"> IS the painting; clicking it summons the operating system's native colour dialog, which floods the viewport and theme-color with a single chosen monochrome.

title: Afterimage (Not on This Page)
source: Jasper Johns, Flag (1954-55); Jasper Johns, afterimage flag demonstration; Ewald Hering, opponent-process theory of colour vision
mechanism: Timed two-state surface: each visit randomly picks one of sixteen flags (built as inline SVG in per-channel inverted colours) and rotates it to a random angle; 20s fixation on a centred dot, then a crossfade to a neutral field where the opponent-process afterimage forms in the viewer's eye, not on screen.

title: Un Coup de Dés (le hasard n'est pas aboli)
source: Marcel Broodthaers, Un Coup de Dés Jamais N'Abolira Le Hasard (Image) (1969); Stéphane Mallarmé, Un Coup de Dés Jamais N'Abolira Le Hasard (1897); net.art (browser layout engine as material)
mechanism: Words rendered as opaque bars via color:transparent on their own black inline-boxes, still selectable/copyable/in-source, with browser reflow re-throwing the constellation and a resize counter.

title: I Do Not Wish to Add Any More
source: Douglas Huebler, statement for January 5-31, 1969 (Seth Siegelaub); Lawrence Weiner, Declaration of Intent (1968); net.art (the DOM as material)
mechanism: A MutationObserver removes any newly added DOM element (including console-appended nodes) while a tally counts refusals, never additions.

title: Truisms (Tab)
source: Jenny Holzer, Truisms (1977-79); Jenny Holzer, Spectacolor LED board, Times Square (1982); net.art (the scrolling-title trick / browser chrome as material)
mechanism: A character-clock marquee streams appropriated truisms through document.title, which persists across tab-switches as the web's public signage.

title: Concetto Spaziale, «Attese»
source: Lucio Fontana, Concetto Spaziale, «Attese» (1958-1968); Lucio Fontana, Spatialism / White Manifesto (1946); net.art (the document plane as material)
mechanism: Pointer-drag appends a vesica to an evenodd clip-path, punching real holes in the coloured document plane so a black void layer behind is revealed; capped at seven, irreversible per visit, reload heals; no storage, no network.

title: Hammer Price
source: The Robert & Ethel Scull collection sale, Sotheby Parke-Bernet, New York, 18 October 1973; Robert Rauschenberg; Marcel Duchamp / the readymade
mechanism: An <input type=range> bid against a per-visit hidden reserve; crossing it greys the canvas, veils it as 'withdrawn to a private collection,' and settles a live ledger (hammer price, consignor's profit, artist $0) — client-side only, no storage, no network.

title: Verb List (Actions to Relate to a Page)
source: Richard Serra, Verb List Compilation: Actions to Relate to Oneself (1967-68); Process art / Anti-Form; Lawrence Weiner, Declaration of Intent (1968); net.art (CSS transforms and the DOM as material)
mechanism: A menu of transitive verbs (to twist, to smear, to scatter, to remove) each triggers its literal CSS transform/filter or DOM mutation on the slab, accumulating per click; reload resets, no storage, no network.

title: Following Piece (Nothing Recorded)
source: Vito Acconci, Following Piece (1969); net.art / mouse-tracking surveillance analytics
mechanism: pointermove (the analytics/heatmap primitive) drives an easing cursor-pursuit that ends on mouseout/blur ('private space'); no cookie, storage, network, or log — the ledger reads 0 bytes and resets on reload.

title: I Am Sitting in a Room (Re-encoded)
source: Alvin Lucier, I Am Sitting in a Room (1969); net.art / generational loss (the re-uploaded, re-encoded file); JPEG / discrete cosine transform basis functions
mechanism: Recursive client-side canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg') feedback loop (re-encode + slight zoom/rotate each generation) whose accumulating 8x8 DCT block artifacts are the medium's resonant modes.

title: 3 Standard Stoppages (Reference Pixel)
source: Marcel Duchamp, 3 Standard Stoppages (1913-14); the CSS reference pixel (1in = 96px, CSS Values); Mel Bochner, Measurement series
mechanism: Per-visit Math.random drops three threads of true arc-length 96px (the CSS reference inch); each crumpled chord is adopted as a unit and divides window.innerWidth live on resize, so one exact pixel width yields three quarrelling measurements.

title: Not Your Backdrop
source: Mark Rothko, Seagram Murals (1958-59); The Four Seasons / Seagram Building commission, withdrawn by the artist 1959; net.art frame-busting; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: Frame-bust detection (window.self !== window.top) blanks the painting to a refusal when iframed; a button feeds the page's own source to an inline <iframe srcdoc> copy that withdraws on cue, no network.

title: The Responsive Eye
source: Bridget Riley, Blaze (1962); The Responsive Eye, MoMA (1965); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: requestAnimationFrame rotates a sub-pixel radial grating drawn at the live devicePixelRatio so the moire is interference with the device's physical pixel grid; prefers-reduced-motion freezes it into its own corpse.

title: Merda d'artista (Do Not Open)
source: Piero Manzoni, Merda d'artista (1961); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; Marcel Duchamp, infrathin
mechanism: The native <details>/<summary> disclosure widget IS the tin; its toggle event collapses a live gold-pegged price to $0.00, irreversibly per visit.

title: Vir Heroicus Sublimis (Overflow)
source: Barnett Newman; Vir Heroicus Sublimis (1950-51); Onement I (1948); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art (browser chrome as material)
mechanism: The native vertical scrollbar, present only because the document overflows the viewport (CSS overflow), is styled via ::-webkit-scrollbar and scrollbar-color to be the zip; an overlay-detection script repaints it where the OS hides it.

title: We Value Your Privacy
source: Hans Haacke, MoMA Poll (1970); Hans Haacke / institutional critique; Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; the EU GDPR / ePrivacy cookie-consent banner
mechanism: A real <dialog> showModal() consent banner whose buttons and toggles are dead no-ops, beside a live readout of document.cookie, localStorage/sessionStorage length and performance resource entries — all verified zero whatever you click.

title: What You See Is What You See
source: Frank Stella, Black Paintings (1958-60); Frank Stella, "What you see is what you see" (1966 interview with Bruce Glaser); net.art
mechanism: Canvas redraws concentric bands derived solely from window.innerWidth/innerHeight, re-deducing the composition on every resize; no image data, no network, no storage.

title: Salon des Refusés
source: Salon des Refusés, Paris 1863; Edouard Manet, Le Dejeuner sur l'herbe (1863); Academie des Beaux-Arts / the Salon jury; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: A client-side jury reads live browser facts (document.contentType, devicePixelRatio, the costless Ctrl/Cmd+S copy) against the 1863 academic demands, fails every one, and CSS-flips the canvas to stamp a red R on its reverse — refusal honestly derived from the medium, no storage, no network.

title: Interaction of Color
source: Josef Albers, Interaction of Color (1963); Josef Albers, Homage to the Square (1950–1976); simultaneous (lightness) contrast
mechanism: getComputedStyle attests both chips share one RGB value while two per-visit HSL grounds force simultaneous contrast; a transform-driven converge onto a neutral field proves sameness — a motion impossible on paper.

title: Sallie Gardner at a Gallop
source: Eadweard Muybridge, Sallie Gardner at a Gallop / The Horse in Motion (1878); Eadweard Muybridge, zoopraxiscope; Martin Creed, Work No. 227 / y-a-v-a, The webpage going on and off (2023)
mechanism: Native scroll position is read live and quantized to 12 frames driving a deterministic kinematic gait on canvas — no autoplay, no timer, no stored frames; motion exists only in the act of scrolling.

title: The Artist Is Present
source: Marina Abramović, The Artist Is Present (MoMA, 2010); Vito Acconci, Following Piece (1969)
mechanism: Interaction events (pointermove/wheel/keydown/touch) reset a stillness clock while blur/visibilitychange empty the seat; nothing is stored, logged, or sent.

title: No. 5 (Authenticated)
source: Jackson Pollock, No. 5, 1948; Richard P. Taylor, R. Micolich & D. Jonas, fractal analysis of Pollock (Nature, 1999); K. Jones-Smith & H. Mathur, rebuttal (Nature, 2006); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade
mechanism: Canvas per-visit drip painting whose own ImageData is read back and box-counted client-side for fractal dimension D, self-issuing a certificate that always passes.

title: A Humument (Select to Treat)
source: Tom Phillips, A Humument (1966– ); W. H. Mallock, A Human Document (1892); erasure / found poetry; Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; net.art (Selection API as material)
mechanism: The Selection API (selectionchange + suppressed ::selection): selected words survive as ink, all others recede into a per-visit ground; nothing stored, no network.

title: 手卷 — Never Seen Whole
source: Wang Ximeng, A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains (千里江山圖), 1113; the Chinese handscroll (手卷) format; net.art (the scroll axis as material)
mechanism: A single horizontal overflow-x scroller far wider than the viewport, opened at its rightmost edge, with a per-visit canvas ink landscape whose very length of silk is cut to a random distance on every load (no two scrolls run the same); the browser crop enacts the handscroll's arm's-length viewing and a live meter proves you never see more than one length at once.

title: De Divina Proportione (Drag to Find It)
source: Luca Pacioli & Leonardo da Vinci, De divina proportione (1509); the golden-ratio-in-art myth (Le Corbusier's Modulor, the Parthenon legend); Marcel Duchamp, infrathin
mechanism: Native CSS resize:both handle plus a ResizeObserver measuring the live width/height ratio against phi, with a whirling-squares canvas subdivision that only nests cleanly at the divine proportion.

title: An Oak Tree (Accessible Name)
source: Michael Craig-Martin, An Oak Tree (1973); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; Arthur Danto, The Transfiguration of the Commonplace (1981); HTML alt attribute / the accessible name (WAI)
mechanism: An image's aria-label / accessible name (read live from the DOM) is flipped from 'A glass of water' to 'An oak tree' while the SVG stays byte-identical; no storage, no network.

title: Fountain (As Manufactured)
source: Marcel Duchamp, Fountain (1917); R. Mutt (Duchamp pseudonym); Society of Independent Artists, New York (1917); net.art / the browser default widget as material
mechanism: A deliberately unstyled native <input type=range> rotated via CSS, whose entire appearance is supplied per-device by the browser vendor, with the manufacturer named locally from the UA string.

title: House (Cast of This Room)
source: Rachel Whiteread, Ghost (1990); Rachel Whiteread, House (1993); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: getBoundingClientRect measures each text block live, a canvas fills the emptiness and clears those boxes as voids, then the DOM room is removed so the frozen bitmap no longer reflows on resize.

title: I Went (:visited)
source: On Kawara, I Went (1968-1979); On Kawara, I Read / I Met; CSS :visited history-sniffing mitigation (L. D. Baron / Mozilla, 2010)
mechanism: Same-page hash links become :visited on click (violet to the viewer) while getComputedStyle is forced by the browser's history-sniffing mitigation to always report them as unvisited, so a live detector reads zero.

title: The Creative Act
source: Marcel Duchamp, "The Creative Act" (1957); Umberto Eco, The Open Work / Opera aperta (1962); net.art (IntersectionObserver / ad-viewability tracking as material)
mechanism: IntersectionObserver's intersectionRatio draws a per-visit generative composition in exact proportion to how much of the frame is in the spectator's view; scroll away and it un-paints — no storage, no network.

title: Silencio
source: Eugen Gomringer, silencio (1954); Concrete poetry / Konkrete Poesie; CSS white-space property; net.art (source-vs-render as material)
mechanism: CSS white-space:normal collapses the source's authored whitespace grid (hole intact in view-source), a toggle to white-space:pre restores it — no network, no storage.

title: Artist's Statement
source: Alix Rule & David Levine, "International Art English" (Triple Canopy, 2012); Marcel Duchamp, the readymade; y-a-v-a, Modernipsum (2012); Roland Barthes, The Death of the Author (1967)
mechanism: A native <datalist> autocomplete presents a closed, finite lexicon of International Art English as un-restylable browser chrome; authorship becomes selection, with a live tally grading fluency, nothing stored or sent.

title: Bicho (Critter)
source: Lygia Clark, Bicho (1960); Neo-Concrete Manifesto / Ferreira Gullar (1959); Marcel Duchamp, The Creative Act (1957); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: A forward-kinematic linkage driven solely by pointer events (no rAF, no autoplay, no storage); motion exists only during manipulation, and each load re-mints a random, unrepeatable animal.

title: Round as Giotto's O
source: Giotto di Bondone; Giorgio Vasari, Le Vite de' più eccellenti pittori (1550); the proverb 'rounder than Giotto's O'
mechanism: Pointer-drawn path fitted to a circle client-side (centroid + radial standard deviation); the identical scorer emits and grades the machine's flawless circle, stamped 'not a drawing'. No storage, no network.

title: Arranged According to the Laws of Chance
source: Hans (Jean) Arp, Untitled (Collage with Squares Arranged According to the Laws of Chance), 1916-17; Dada chance operations; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Kenneth Martin, Chance and Order / y-a-v-a, A Chance of Order (2021)
mechanism: crypto.getRandomValues() drives a per-throw canvas collage held only in RAM (no seed, no storage, no network), making the picture physically irreproducible.

title: Anonyme Skulpturen (o. O.)
source: Bernd & Hilla Becher, Typologies / Anonyme Skulpturen (Water Towers); The Dusseldorf School of photography; Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: Client-side canvas procedurally draws twelve frontally-framed water-tower silhouettes in a fixed grid, held only in RAM (no storage, no seed, no network), so reload destroys the plate irreversibly.

title: Narrow Symbol
source: Andy Warhol, Dollar Sign (1981); J.S.G. Boggs (hand-drawn currency); Alexander Brener / Malevich defacement (1997); y-a-v-a, Art is Money (2013)
mechanism: Intl.NumberFormat currency formatting (narrowSymbol) denominates a constant integer in the viewer's locale-guessed currency, live and offline, so value becomes pure typography with no rate to reconcile it.

title: Vanitas (Charge Remaining)
source: Dutch vanitas still life; Harmen Steenwyck; Pieter Claesz; the Battery Status API and its removal for fingerprinting; Felix Gonzalez-Torres, "Untitled" (Perfect Lovers)
mechanism: navigator.getBattery() level/charging events drive a canvas candle flame; the anti-tracking removal of the API in Firefox/Safari leaves the vanitas unable to read your device's mortality.

title: Not in the Dictionary
source: Kurt Schwitters, Merz (1919); Dada / Zaum / the manifesto neologism; Marcel Duchamp, infrathin; y-a-v-a, Modernipsum (2012)
mechanism: A live contenteditable element with spellcheck='true': the OS spellchecker paints red squiggles under art's neologisms — marks rendered outside the DOM that expose nothing to JavaScript, so a real DOM search for the flags returns zero.

title: Unreachable
source: Jean Tinguely, Homage to New York (1960); the vanitas / memento mori tradition; Marcel Duchamp, the infrathin; ECMAScript WeakRef / FinalizationRegistry (TC39, 2021)
mechanism: WeakRef + FinalizationRegistry: dropping the last strong pointer makes the work unreachable, and non-deterministic JS garbage collection (detected via weak.deref() and the registry callback) enacts its death.

title: The Difference (after Sturtevant)
source: Elaine Sturtevant, Warhol Flowers (1964-65); Andy Warhol, Flowers (1964); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
mechanism: Canvas globalCompositeOperation='difference' subtracts a draggable copy from its identical original, with a live getImageData pixel count reporting fidelity vs. visible art.

title: Touch Piece (Do Not Look)
source: Yoko Ono, Grapefruit instruction pieces (1964); Lucy Lippard, Six Years: The Dematerialization of the Art Object (1966-72)
mechanism: navigator.vibrate performs a crypto-random per-visit score gated behind a user gesture; feature detection decides whether the work exists at all; nothing rendered as the work, no storage, no network.

title: In Praise of Laziness
source: Mladen Stilinovic, In Praise of Laziness (1993); Lee Lozano, General Strike Piece (1969); Marcel Duchamp / the readymade
mechanism: requestIdleCallback paints a stroke as long as deadline.timeRemaining(); didTimeout ticks (busy main thread) add no paint, so interaction starves the work.

title: Département des Aigles (In the Crates)
source: Marcel Broodthaers, Musée d'Art Moderne, Département des Aigles, Section des Figures (1968-72); Marcel Broodthaers, "Ceci n'est pas un objet d'art" label; René Magritte, The Treachery of Images (1929); Bernd & Hilla Becher / typology
mechanism: HTML <template> elements: their eagle SVGs are parsed into inert fragments that are present in the DOM (counted and measured live) but structurally never rendered, so the walls stay empty.

title: The Most Reproduced Image
source: Marcel Duchamp, Fountain (1917); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Andy Warhol; Olia Lialina & Dragan Espenschied, One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age (net.art broken-image tradition)
mechanism: Intentionally invalid inline data-URI sources fail locally so each browser engine substitutes its own broken-image placeholder; a Reproduce button clones editions in RAM only, zero network.

title: With My Back to the World (Graphite on Pixels)
source: Agnes Martin; Agnes Martin, With My Back to the World (1997); the raster pixel grid / devicePixelRatio; net.art
mechanism: Canvas draws a per-visit sub-pixel graphite tremor that devicePixelRatio quantizes into grey squares; a native nearest-neighbour magnifier reads the backing store to expose the loss.

title: Indivisible
source: Augusto de Campos and the Noigandres group / Brazilian concrete poetry (1950s); Marcel Duchamp, infrathin
mechanism: CSS hyphens:auto forces the layout engine's per-language hyphenation dictionary to insert render-only break-hyphens absent from the DOM; lang switch and resize re-break the same words differently.

title: I Am Still Alive (Caret)
source: On Kawara, I Am Still Alive (1970– ); Marcel Duchamp, infrathin (inframince); net.art (the OS-drawn caret as material)
mechanism: A focused contenteditable field that refuses all input; the caret's blink interval and on/off state are supplied by the OS and never exposed to JavaScript, and blur/tab-switch stops it — no timer, no storage, no network.

title: COPY / COPY
source: Marcel Duchamp, inframince / infrathin (c. 1935); Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935); Sherrie Levine, After Walker Evans (1981); Unicode confusables / IDN homograph attack (net.art)
mechanism: Unicode confusables (Latin vs Cyrillic homoglyphs) render identically while JS string comparison and normalize() expose a permanent byte-level difference the eye and paper cannot see.

title: Infra-mince (Enforced)
source: Marcel Duchamp, inframince / infra-mince (notes, c. 1935); Spectre / Meltdown timer-resolution reduction shipped by browser vendors (2018); Mel Bochner, Measurement series (1968-69)
mechanism: performance.now() resolution clamping and jitter (the post-Spectre anti-timing-attack mitigation) sampled in a tight rAF loop to reveal the smallest interval the browser will admit, drawn as a comb histogram.

title: Print Gallery (The Part It Cannot Draw)
source: M. C. Escher, Prentententoonstelling (Print Gallery), 1956; the Droste effect; Hendrik Lenstra, mathematical completion of Escher's Print Gallery (2003); net.art (the page as its own material)
mechanism: An <iframe srcdoc> fed the document's own outerHTML nests the page inside itself in a Droste spiral; the browser's finite same-origin frame-nesting depth is the unresolvable hole.

title: Not to Be Shown
source: Hilma af Klint; Hilma af Klint, The Ten Largest / Paintings for the Temple (1907); Hilma af Klint's instruction to withhold her work for 20 years after death; Marcel Duchamp, infrathin (inframince); On Kawara, Today series
mechanism: A live new Date() comparison against a fixed release date (checked on load, on visibilitychange, and every second) gates whether the canvas composition draws at all; before release only a seal and countdown show, and the page states the lock is defeated by advancing the system clock.
